answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before joining a mesa of reviewers; opening many identities then ties up capital, and cheating risks losing it when independent reviewers expose duplicate behavior. A grove of diverse reviewers can compare histories, while an echo of the same claims across new accounts raises suspicion. This raises the cost of Sybil attacks, but wealthy attackers or colluding reviewers can still evade detection.
